parsed.attack: The invite loop is the best acquisition structure in the batch - one bought install seeds three lock screens, so effective CPI per member falls from $5.84 to about $1.95 - but you monetise the group, not the member, so the division is illusory. At a $3.99/month group price ($3.39 net) and their own 3% conversion floor, the acquiring sibling still costs $195 on iOS and $64 on Android per paying group: 57 and 19 months of unbroken group retention against kill line 2, which already concedes entries may fall below one per member per week by week 6. And the PCC small-developer free tier is a subsidy, not a cost structure: summarising every logged call is free only until volume exceeds the allowance, at which point a per-call cost arrives against $1.13 of monthly revenue per member.
parsed.strongest_defence: Zero marginal cost while small means organic installs are pure margin, invite_for_function genuinely delivers two free members per paid one, and caregiver Facebook groups are a dense unpaid channel; price the group at $7.99 rather than $3.99 - it is a household splitting one obligation, not three individuals - and the per-group economics land inside the median payer band.
parsed.verdict_reason: Margin holds while small, but per-group revenue of $3.39 net against a $64-195 acquisition cost per paying group needs 19-57 months of retention on a product whose own kill line expects decay by week 6.
